author: rodboev
body:
When the target messages are already known, there's no way to stage them from the CLI. A script or agent holding internal message IDs (from prior search output, a triage journal, or a `show-deletion` review) has to reconstruct a search query and hope it selects exactly those messages:

```bash
msgvault stage-delete --ids 123,456,789
msgvault stage-delete --ids 123,456,789 --dry-run
```

Neither works today; `stage-delete` accepts only a query argument plus `--dry-run` and `--source-id`.

## Proposal

Add an `--ids` flag taking comma-separated internal message IDs, mutually exclusive with the query argument. It submits through the existing `message_ids` field of `POST /api/v1/deletions`, which already resolves live Gmail targets authoritatively (live rows, Gmail source, provider message ID required), so it needs no search, FTS, or analytical-cache involvement and no new validation surface, and it inherits the field's existing engine support (SQLite or Parquet data). `--dry-run`, the manifest format, `show-deletion`, and `delete-staged` behave exactly as they do for the query form.

This is the remaining slice of #191, which proposed both the query form (shipped in #759) and this one.
title: stage-delete: the --ids form from #191 is not implemented
